summary: Active fixed-white light on a cliff at the entrance to Leonardville Harbour, Deer Island, New Brunswick; built 1913-14 and kept by the Coast Guard, closed to visitors.

structures.note: White pyramid tower with red top (CCG list: 8.5 m structure height). LighthouseFriends: 27 ft (8.2 m), square with sloping sides. Rowlett: 8 m (28 ft), square pyramidal wood, painted white with red trim. Built 1913 (LighthouseFriends) or 1914 (Rowlett).

access.note: Canadian Coast Guard property. Grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends); site and tower closed, private property (Rowlett). Visible through trees from NB 772.

visit.note: Grounds and tower closed. Deer Island reached by ferry from L'Etete and from Campobello Island (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Tower erected under contract by A. L. Mury, West Arichat, for $896, with a 6th order dioptric lens (LighthouseFriends; Department report for the year ended 30 June 1914 lists the contract). Rowlett gives 1914.
Alonzo Conley appointed keeper, 20 December 1913 (Department keepers' list, year ended 30 June 1915; position-matched).
Keeper Conley reports a large meteor fall into the sea off Harbour-de-Lute, Campobello Island, relayed to the meteorological department in Toronto (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: Alonzo H. Conley
keepers.note: First keeper (LighthouseFriends). Department keepers' list gives appointment 20 December 1913 at $230 (position-matched; page image read). LighthouseFriends says 'at least 1936'.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends says the tower was erected in 1913 under the Mury contract. Rowlett and Wikidata give 1914. The Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1914 records the contract among that year's new aids, and its keeper was appointed 20 December 1913, which fits a completed tower in late 1913. Recorded as 1913 with the disagreement noted.
CCG list gives 20.0 m (matches the record). LighthouseFriends gives 59 ft (18 m) and Rowlett 20 m (66 ft). CCG and Rowlett agree on 20 m.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate evidence: LighthouseFriends (keeper and build detail, 1936 letter, access), Rowlett (1914 date, dimensions, access), the CCG list (current characteristic, focal height, year-round status) and two Department reports. Verified 2026-10-28 by the fact-checker as page images: the FY1914 new-aids table (report scan 49, printed p.42) puts 'A. L. Mury, West Arch-ichat, Contract price $896' on the same row as 'Erection of a wooden lighthouse tower and installation of a 6th order dioptric lens' for Leonardville, so the contract match is confirmed. The story spells the town 'West Arichat' as the Department prints it in its FY1912 and FY1914 reports; LighthouseFriends writes 'West Archichat'. The FY1915 keepers' list (scan 73) puts 'Alonzo Conley, Dec. 20, 1913, 230 00' on the Leonardville row (the row directly above 'Lepreau'), so the position match is confirmed. The FY1917 table (scan 116) is not a keepers' list: it is the 'List of Wharves and Wharfingers' (Sessional Paper 21). Its Leonardville row names no wharfinger; 'Vacant.' sits against Little Aldouane, and the 15 Nov 1915 appointment belongs to A. J. Fraser at Loggieville. The earlier reading that tied a 1915 vacancy to Leonardville was wrong, and the story no longer cites it. Charlotte County is confirmed by Rowlett's section heading. Focal plane: LighthouseFriends 59 ft; Rowlett and CCG 20 m. The record's 'access: closed' is supported. The Coast Guard owns the light per LighthouseFriends and Rowlett, not the CCG list. The LighthouseFriends 1936 meteor account is known only through LighthouseFriends; no archive copy was checked. The Passamaquoddy border statement is Rowlett's general context, not a station fact. No wrecks or storms tied to the station were found in the local Department reports (1900-1924).
